# ERN about page. Edit the copy here, then rebuild:
#
#     quarto render about.qmd
#
# That overwrites about.html in place. git is the safety net — review
# `git diff about.html` before committing.
#
# The page chrome lives in _extensions/ern/about/template.html, which also
# carries the standing constraints on where Berkeley, BIDS, and the federal
# seals may appear. Read those comments before moving a logo between walls.
#
# NOTE: values here are parsed as Markdown. Write &#39; for a straight
# apostrophe, which is what the rest of the site uses. Do not backslash-escape:
# inside a folded block scalar (>-) YAML keeps the backslash and it lands on
# the page. Colons and URLs need no escaping.
# ============================================================================

hero:
  eyebrow: "About"
  # Rewritten 2026-10-08 at Tim's direction and approved by him the same day.
  # The earlier headlines ("No federal agency counts evictions. We do.", live
  # since Aug 10; "We make things that can't be unseen", the team's 2026 page)
  # were retired as campy. The register is plain and academic: the site is
  # public-facing and exists to give advocates tools and policymakers an
  # understanding of trends. ERN's framing is making eviction understandable
  # through accessible maps and trends, not a claim to be the only counter.
  h1_lead: "Making eviction"
  h1_em: "understandable."
  lede: >-
    The Eviction Research Network collects eviction court records across the
    United States and turns them into maps, state profiles, and trend data that
    anyone can read. We are a research program at UC Berkeley, founded in
    2018, and we work with courts, legal aid organizations, public agencies,
    advocates, and universities to show where evictions happen, who they fall
    on, and how they change over time.

mission:
  eyebrow: "Mission"
  # Rewritten 2026-10-08 in the plain register. The facts are the team's
  # (f725271, 23 Feb 2026): the King County case, the four- and five-fold
  # disparities, the Washington notice period, and Baltimore's right to
  # counsel. The em-dashes and the consultant phrasing are gone.
  h2_lead: "Where the work"
  h2_em: "began."
  paragraphs:
    - >-
      The network began with one case in King County, Washington. A mother was
      served an eviction notice, settled out of court, and stayed in her home
      for two more years. The filing stayed on her record and was later used to
      deny her housing. With support from the American Civil Liberties Union,
      her case raised a larger question about who faces eviction and how those
      cases are recorded.
    - >-
      Research in King County found that Black households were four times more
      likely than White households to receive an eviction notice, and that
      Black women were five times more likely than White men to have an
      eviction case filed against them. Tim Thomas, who founded ERN, led that
      research and extended it across Washington State and then to other
      states. The findings informed Washington&#39;s 2019 extension of the
      eviction notice period from 3 to 14 days and Baltimore City&#39;s right
      to counsel for tenants facing eviction.
    - >-
      The same patterns appear in state after state, and they follow lines
      drawn by earlier housing policy, including redlining. Because a stable
      home shapes health, schooling, and work, eviction reaches well beyond the
      courtroom. ERN exists to make those patterns visible. We collect court
      records, standardize them, and publish maps and trends that show where
      evictions are concentrated, who they fall on, and how they change over
      time, so that tenants, advocates, agencies, and researchers can see the
      problem in their own communities and act on it.
  image:
    src: "images/about_page/blackandwhitezone.jpeg"
    # The old page called this a map of a redlined zone. It is a photograph.
    alt: >-
      Black and white aerial photograph of a lakeside city, dense residential
      blocks running back from the shoreline toward a distant downtown

work:
  eyebrow: "What we do"
  h2_lead: "What"
  h2_em: "we do."
  # Rewritten 2026-10-08 in the plain register. The four card titles are the
  # team's, Advocacy included (Tim restored it from "Policy evidence" on
  # 2026-08-24). The bodies now say what each line of work produces.
  sub: >-
    We collect, analyze, and map eviction data, and we help courts, agencies,
    and partner organizations do the same with theirs.
  image:
    src: "images/about_page/gimmeshelter.jpeg"
    # The old page called this demonstrators with signs. It is a shop sign.
    alt: >-
      A hanging shop sign reading Gimme Shelter above a neighborhood sidewalk
  capabilities:
    - title: "Data preparation"
      icon: "layers"
      body: >-
        We collect, clean, and standardize eviction records for the courts,
        agencies, and organizations that hold them but do not have the staff or
        tools to turn them into usable data.
    - title: "Maps and analysis"
      icon: "map"
      body: >-
        We measure filing and judgment rates by neighborhood and by race and
        sex, and publish the results as state profiles, interactive maps, and
        trend charts that a reader without a statistics background can follow.
    - title: "Network"
      icon: "people"
      body: >-
        We work alongside courts, legal aid organizations, agencies, advocates,
        and universities, helping partners understand their own data and sharing
        our methods and code so that findings can be checked, repeated, and
        extended.
    - title: "Advocacy"
      icon: "megaphone"
      body: >-
        We bring the evidence to legislators, agencies, and courts, and we
        advise on policies that reduce preventable evictions and their
        disproportionate impact on vulnerable communities.
